chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Maryam Al-Ansari, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the boy who had not yet reached puberty (had not bed-wetted), if he slanders a man, would he be whipped? He (peace be upon him) said: No, and that is because if a man slandered the boy, he would not be whipped (either).

key_terms.يَقْذِفَ: slanders (specifically in the context of hadd al-qadhf)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for a pre-pubescent boy who slanders someone?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes that a pre-pubescent boy (ghulam) is exempt from the hadd punishment of qadhf (flogging), emphasizing that legal accountability for this specific penalty requires full maturity. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between general moral responsibility and the specific conditions required for applying corporal hadd penalties, ensuring symmetry in legal judgment between accuser and accused regarding age. The narration underscores the principle that the hadd for slander is not merely a reflection of the act but is contingent upon the legal capacity (ahliyyah) of the perpetrator.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Abu Maryam Al Ansary who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the boy who had not yet bed wetted, slanders the man, would he be whipped?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, and that, had the man slandered the boy, he would not be whipped (either)’.
